name: Appalachian Excellence; Chancellor's (Wilson unconfirmed)
value: Appalachian Excellence: up to $3,000 per year for in-state students or $4,000 per year for out-of-state students. Chancellor’s: full tuition, fees, housing, and a meal plan for up to eight semesters, plus a funded first-year study abroad experience. Renewal GPA and Appalachian Excellence duration are not stated on the current pages.
deadline: Submit admission by November 15. Honors pages conflict: the first-year application page, which displays the 2027 Honors essay prompt, says submit the Honors essay by November 15, while the Chancellor’s page says November 30. The Chancellor’s page lists January 24 virtual interviews and March 31 scholarship acceptance, without cycle years. Confirm the applicable 2027 deadlines in MyMountaineer.
apply: Appalachian Excellence consideration is automatic for academically qualified students meeting admission deadlines. Apply to the Honors College through the MyMountaineer Honors essay for automatic Chancellor’s consideration; finalists interview virtually. The financial aid directory still refers to additional portal steps, so follow the current portal instructions.
eligibility: Entering first-year students. The Honors application requires at least a 3.5 unweighted high school GPA; this threshold applies to Chancellor’s consideration, not necessarily Appalachian Excellence. Chancellor’s Scholars participate in Honors and work toward University Honors requirements. First-year Honors students generally live in Cone Hall with an Honors roommate.
notes: These are distinct awards with different coverage and application routes. Wilson is not identified as a current award on the pages reviewed. Honors requires a thesis and an international education experience, which can include approved alternatives to study abroad.

name: John M. Belk Scholarship
value: Comprehensive tuition, fees, housing, and food for four years, plus special opportunity stipends. Current official pages conflict on the stipend total: $10,000 on the nomination directory and $6,000 on the general scholarship page. Eight scholars are named in each entering class.
deadline: For high school graduates in 2027, nomination is due November 1, 2026; admission application November 15, 2026; supporting documents November 30, 2026. Published selection stages run from February semifinalist interviews through March finalist interviews, with awards by April 1; exact 2027 interview dates are not stated.
apply: A school counselor, principal/head of school, or community-based college access program representative may nominate up to two students using the official form. Davidson admission staff may also nominate strong applicants. Submit the admission application and required supporting documents, including recommendations, then participate in semifinalist and finalist interviews if selected.
eligibility: Entering first-year students with outstanding academic accomplishment, character, leadership, and service. Domestic and international high schools or eligible college access programs may nominate. Renewal for the remaining three years requires the established GPA, progress toward degree, award-specific conditions, and full participation in college life; the numerical GPA is not published on these pages.
notes: The November 15 scholarship application deadline does not itself require selecting binding Early Decision. Confirm the stipend allocation and renewal GPA with the scholarship office.

name: Robertson Scholars Leadership Program
value: Eight semesters of full tuition, room, board, and most mandatory fees, with funding for up to three summer experiences, conferences, and up to two semesters abroad. Renewal requires a 3.0 GPA at the end of the first year and 3.30 at the end of each subsequent academic year, plus required program participation.
deadline: Early notification application: October 15, 2026. Regular application: November 15, 2026. Group activities December 2026–February 2027; semifinalist interviews February 2027; finalist interviews early March 2027; recipient campus visits March 31–April 3, 2027. Apply separately to Duke and/or UNC by each university’s admission deadline. FAQ lists midnight on November 15 without a time zone.
apply: Submit the separate Robertson application and apply to Duke and/or UNC in the same year. No nomination and no scholarship transcript submission. Applicants who have taken SAT or ACT must report scores. Exactly one leadership-focused recommendation is required; the recommender submits it through a unique application link. More than one letter is not accepted. Letters should not be from friends, peers, family or family friends, and applicants must not email or fax letters directly. Selected applicants complete a group activity and semifinalist/finalist interviews.
eligibility: First-year undergraduate applicants who have not matriculated at another university; transfer and graduate applicants are ineligible. All citizenships and nationalities may apply; international applicants must be able to obtain a U.S. study visa. No preferred state of residence or required major. A gap-year student already admitted to Duke or UNC must wait until matriculation to apply through the current-student route.
notes: Scholars matriculate at one university, take at least five courses at the sister institution, and participate in campus switch, retreats, community events, and Community Summer. Admission to either university is required to receive its award; school-specific finalist invitations apply. Applying ED elsewhere is allowed, but notify Robertson if admitted under a binding commitment.

provider: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
name: Morehead-Cain Scholarship
value: Four-year educational program covering tuition, books, room and board and/or a semester stipend, plus a four-year Summer Enrichment Program and discovery opportunities. An optional gap year is offered. Scholars follow Morehead-Cain Community Standards; recipient-specific terms are communicated through the scholar network.
deadline: Direct scholarship application and all counselor/recommendation materials: October 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EST, as stated by the sponsor. Out-of-state school nominations: June 30, 2026. UNC application: October 15, 2026 for Early Action or January 1, 2027 for scholarship candidates using Regular Decision. Semifinalist notification and video interviews December 2026; finalist notification January 2027; FACE January–February 2027; final selection February 26–March 1, 2027; recipient notification March 5, 2027; acceptance April 5, 2027. Admissions Referral Program uses a separate timeline.
apply: Apply separately to Morehead-Cain and UNC. North Carolina residents or North Carolina high school students may self-nominate; other direct applicants need an eligible school or affiliate nomination. Out-of-state schools may nominate two seniors. Enter counselor and recommender details, school information, senior courses, and essay responses; all supporting materials are due with the application. Semifinalists interview by video and finalists attend selection stages.
eligibility: On track to graduate high school in spring and competitive for UNC admission. Out-of-state and international direct applicants need a nominating school or affiliate. Eligible applicants attending school outside North Carolina who are not North Carolina residents may instead be referred through UNC Early Action by October 15, 2026; referral is not guaranteed. Test optional for 2026–27. Selection assesses leadership, character, scholarship, and physical vigor.
notes: The Admissions Referral Program has a different application timeline; applicants not contacted by mid-December are not advancing. Applying binding ED elsewhere is allowed, but notify the foundation if admitted; unsuccessful ED applicants remaining in the process may not apply binding ED II. The sponsor calls its October deadline time zone EST; confirm the portal time if needed.

provider: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
name: Levine Scholars
value: Tuition, housing, meals, books and mandatory fees for four years, plus summer experiences and an $8,000 community-project grant.
deadline: Nomination or self-nomination: October 15, 2026. Complete UNC Charlotte admission application: November 1, 2026. Levine supplemental application and all three recommendations: November 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EST as stated by the program. Semifinalist notice week of December 7, 2026; finalist notice January 8, 2027; on-campus finalist interviews February 21–22, 2027; recipient notice March 1, 2027; acceptance April 1, 2027.
apply: Receive a counselor/college advisor nomination or self-nominate to access the Levine application. Apply separately to UNC Charlotte by the scholarship’s admission deadline, including fee or waiver, official transcript, and admission essay. The Levine application requires three essay responses, extended answers, activities, and three online recommendations addressing academics, community service, and leadership. Admission recommendation letters are not shared with Levine. Finalists attend campus interviews.
eligibility: U.S. citizens or permanent residents applying for first-year enrollment at UNC Charlotte in the fall immediately after high-school graduation. Gap-year students are not eligible. No minimum GPA is specified; SAT/ACT submission is optional. Admission to UNC Charlotte is required to receive the award.
notes: About 20 entering scholars annually. No required major, North Carolina residency, financial need, or minimum entry GPA. Published academic averages are not eligibility cutoffs. Levine is distinct from Honors; applicants seeking other Honors awards need the separate Honors application, while Levine semifinalists automatically enter University Honors. Numerical award renewal requirements are not stated on the public pages reviewed.

provider: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
name: Honors Scholars Program
value: Four-year Honors awards range from $4,000 per year to full cost of attendance, depending on the named scholarship. Examples include $20,000, $24,000, $30,000, and $40,000 total awards; Class of 1955 offers $4,000 per semester plus potential study abroad and internship funding. Sloan Endowed covers full cost of attendance for Pell-eligible students. Other awards have specific residency, major, or gender criteria.
deadline: Apply to Global Honors by December 1 for scholarship consideration; selected applicants are invited to virtual interviews by January 10, scholarship offers by February 15, and confirm Honors enrollment by May 1. These dates lack cycle years; confirm Fall 2027 dates in the admissions portal. The March 15 regular Honors deadline is not the scholarship priority deadline.
apply: Apply to UNCG, then use the invitation link in the Admissions Portal to submit the Global Honors application with a maximum 500-word essay and current resume. Selected scholarship candidates interview virtually. Up to two admission recommendations are optional and may be reviewed by Honors; there is no required Honors-specific recommendation.
eligibility: Incoming students admitted to Global Honors. First-year eligibility requires 3.8 weighted high school GPA OR SAT 1280 OR ACT 26; tests are optional when qualifying by GPA. A special admission petition is available. Scholarship renewal requires at least 12 credits each semester, at least a 3.3 GPA each term, major satisfactory academic progress, progress toward Honors graduation, program events, and annual director meeting.
notes: This listing covers multiple named Honors scholarships with different amounts and restrictions. Reynolds has its own listing. Full cost of attendance applies to specific awards rather than every Honors Scholar.

provider: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
name: Reynolds Scholarship
value: Reynolds: $4,000 per semester for four years, plus potential additional awards of $2,500 for study abroad, $1,250 for an internship, and $1,250 for a community service project. Maximum listed total is $37,000; the $5,000 additional funding depends on the relevant activities.
deadline: Apply to Global Honors by December 1 for scholarship consideration; selected applicants are invited to virtual interviews by January 10, scholarship offers by February 15, and confirm Honors enrollment by May 1. These dates lack cycle years; confirm Fall 2027 dates in the admissions portal. The March 15 regular Honors deadline is not the scholarship priority deadline.
apply: Apply to UNCG, then use the invitation link in the Admissions Portal to submit the Global Honors application with a maximum 500-word essay and current resume. Selected scholarship candidates interview virtually. Up to two admission recommendations are optional and may be reviewed by Honors; there is no required Honors-specific recommendation.
eligibility: Incoming students admitted to Global Honors. First-year eligibility requires 3.8 weighted high school GPA OR SAT 1280 OR ACT 26; tests are optional when qualifying by GPA. A special admission petition is available. Scholarship renewal requires at least 12 credits each semester, at least a 3.3 GPA each term, major satisfactory academic progress, progress toward Honors graduation, program events, and annual director meeting. Reynolds is restricted to North Carolina residents.
notes: The current incoming-student scholarship directory confirms Reynolds benefits and North Carolina residency. Additional activity funding is potential, rather than an unconditional $5,000 stipend.

name: National Alumni Scholarship
value: Full tuition, related fees, room, and board, renewable up to four years if renewal criteria are met. The current page does not specify the numerical renewal GPA or credit requirements.
deadline: Published National Alumni application window is November 1–January 10 for the 2026–27 academic year, while the general scholarship calendar says December 15. Priority admission is November 1 without a cycle year. Fall 2027 dates have not been confirmed.
apply: Apply for admission and submit the separate National Alumni scholarship application when available. Published requirements include two typed, signed recommendations on official letterhead, including one from a school faculty member or administrator; relatives may not recommend. FAFSA is encouraged for full consideration of financial aid, rather than stated as mandatory for this award.
eligibility: Published 2026–27 requirements: U.S. citizen graduating from an accredited high school before the award fall, university admission requirements, first bachelor’s degree, and at least a 3.75 GPA on a 4.0 scale, with weighting unspecified. ACT/SAT are optional for 2026–27. Fall 2027 criteria are not confirmed.
notes: The separate National Alumni award is distinct from automatic general merit scholarships and geographically restricted alumni chapter awards. Confirm the conflicting application deadline and future eligibility with Financial Aid.

name: Lewis and Elizabeth Dowdy Scholars
value: Full four-year tuition, related fees, room and board with standard double-occupancy housing, for fall and spring semesters only. Funds may support fall/spring study abroad; summer school is excluded. Renewal considers a 3.50 cumulative GPA and hours earned at the end of spring, plus annual Dowdy program participation. The required number of earned hours is not stated.
deadline: Honors Distinguished Scholars application: November 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EST as stated by the university. Finalist notice late January 2027; on-campus Honors Weekend and scholarship interviews February 26–27, 2027; awards mid-March 2027; acceptance April 15, 2027. December 15, 2026 is the Honors-only deadline and does not provide these scholarship considerations.
apply: Submit the university admission application first, then use the specific Honors application link with Aggie Admissions Portal credentials. One Honors application covers Dowdy, Cheatham-White, and February One, with at most one award. Complete a school endorsement or self-nomination, academic/activities information, a 500–1,000-word essay, a roughly 90-second recorded video, and two recommendations; the current admission page says evaluation forms are required and formal letters optional. Finalists interview on campus.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students pursuing a first bachelor's degree with leadership and service, at least 3.75 weighted high-school GPA, and U.S. citizenship or eligible-noncitizen status. The Dowdy page lists SAT 1270 or ACT 27 while also calling tests optional; clarify how that benchmark applies to applicants who omit scores. Honors application by the priority date is required.
notes: Current Dowdy award page expressly limits eligibility to U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens. It lists SAT 1270/ACT 27 as a minimum and in the same line says test optional, so no mandatory score filter is applied here. Renewal considers 3.50 cumulative GPA, earned hours at spring review and annual program participation; the required hour count is not published.

name: Park Scholarships
value: Four-year package valued at about $129,000 for in-state students or $244,000 for out-of-state students in the Class of 2031. Includes tuition, fees, room and board, books, supplies, travel, computer stipend, and personal expenses. Renewable for eight semesters with at least 12 credits per semester and high standards in academics, character, conduct, and program/service participation; a numerical college GPA threshold is not published in the FAQ.
deadline: Both NC State Early Action admission and Park application, including two separate recommendations: November 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Semifinalist notice by December 18, 2026; live Zoom interviews January 16, 2027; finalist notice by February 3, 2027; selection activities in Raleigh March 5–6, 2027; award notice by March 24, 2027.
apply: Apply separately for NC State admission and Park through wolfPAW. Park requires two essays of up to 600 words each, advanced coursework information, and two Park-specific recommendations. Admission recommendations are not shared with Park. The program also reviews the admission essays, activities, honors, transcript, and test scores only if submitted for admission consideration. Selected applicants interview by Zoom and attend finalist selection activities.
eligibility: At least a 3.80 unweighted high school GPA without rounding. Eligible if a U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, OR graduating from a U.S. high school regardless of citizenship. Must apply for fall first-year bachelor’s admission; transfers are ineligible. No required major; SAT/ACT are optional.
notes: The U.S. high school route also permits applicants outside the citizen/permanent-resident categories. Approximately 38 awards are offered. Additional scholarships and need-based grants can reduce Park funding to keep combined aid within cost of attendance. Recommenders cannot be parents/guardians; late or emailed recommendations are not accepted.

name: Merit scholarships (automatic and named programs)
value: Automatic first-year merit tuition awards of $21,000–$26,000 per year for four years, based on high school GPA. The transfer Dean’s Award is $23,000 per year. Competitive named awards provide up to full tuition or full cost of attendance. Renewal follows the scholarship letter; several named awards require full-time campus residence and a 3.0 college GPA.
deadline: Admission decisions are rolling, beginning November 1 before enrollment. There is no separate general merit application deadline. Named scholarship deadlines vary; the catalog lists January 15 for the Davis Art Scholarship without confirming a Fall 2027 cycle date.
apply: Apply through Salem, Common App, or CFNC and provide a high school transcript. All admitted students receive automatic merit consideration. Named art and music awards may require additional materials; contact Admissions for the selected program. Test scores are optional.
eligibility: Salem admits undergraduate students who were assigned female at birth or identify as a woman. First-year automatic merit awards depend on high school GPA; transfer and competitive named awards have separate criteria. Several named awards require full-time campus residence and a 3.0 college GPA for renewal. International applicants have a separate admission route.
notes: This entry groups Salem’s automatic and competitive named scholarships. Current official pages and the 2026–2027 catalog confirm the award family and admission policy. Individual scholarship letters govern renewal, and named awards have different requirements. Fall 2027 dates for named awards remain unconfirmed.

name: Signature scholarships (Reynolds, Carswell, Graylyn, Stamps)
value: Reynolds, Carswell, and Graylyn cover annual tuition, room, and board plus $3,400 for personal expenses; recipients may apply for up to $5,000 in each of three summers. Stamps covers annual tuition, fees, room, and board plus $3,400 for books and personal expenses, and up to $15,000 total for approved enrichment over four years. Exact academic renewal conditions are communicated to recipients.
deadline: Completed admission application by November 15 for automatic Signature scholarship consideration. Finalists interview on campus and are notified by the end of March. These program dates lack cycle years; Fall 2027 dates are not explicitly confirmed.
apply: Submit a complete undergraduate admission application by the scholarship deadline. These Signature programs require no separate scholarship application. Finalists are invited for campus interviews.
eligibility: Entering first-year applicants with exceptional academic promise, leadership, and achievement. Tests are considered if submitted; no numerical academic entry floor is listed. Most merit recipients must remain full-time and live on campus. Current pages do not state a separate citizenship restriction for these four named awards.
notes: These named Signature awards differ in fee coverage, enrichment limits and recipient terms. Up to five Carswell and five Reynolds awards, one Graylyn, and about fifteen Stamps awards are described. The separate need-qualified Leadership and Character Scholarship uses a December 1 admission deadline. Presidential talent scholarship uses a separate application.

name: Presidential Scholarship for Distinguished Achievement
value: Twenty renewable talent scholarships of $16,000 annually. The number of renewal years and award-specific GPA requirements are not stated on the public pages reviewed.
deadline: Separate Presidential application priority deadline November 15; later applications accepted as talent areas allow until the first Sunday after January 1. Finalist interviews by early March, awards late March. Exact Fall 2027 dates are not explicitly stated.
apply: Apply for university admission and submit the separate Presidential application through the student portal. The linked 2026–27 materials guide requires two talent-specific essays of no more than one page each, a document describing submitted talent evidence, and a mentor recommendation. Supply a debate record portfolio, art portfolio, or recordings/work portfolio appropriate to dance, music, or theatre. Finalists interview in person or virtually.
eligibility: Students admitted to Wake Forest with outstanding talent in art, dance, debate, music, or theatre. No required major in the talent area, but active participation in that activity on campus is expected. Most merit awards require full-time enrollment and on-campus housing. No numerical entry academic floor or specific citizenship restriction is published here.
notes: Dance recording 10–12 minutes; music recording 10–15 minutes with contrasting pieces; theatre performance roughly 3–4 minutes with contrasting monologues; visual art portfolio 10–15 works. Debate portfolio includes participation goals, tournaments, preliminary/elimination records, and summer workshops. The guide is an overview; follow portal instructions for the selected talent.

name: General merit
value: Published merit amounts range from $5,000 to full tuition; the range does not specify payment frequency. Admission merit awards are fixed for four years/eight semesters, with cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 and full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits per semester unless a donor specifies different terms.
deadline: Submit the completed admission application by the chosen round: Early Decision I November 15, Early Decision II January 15, or Regular Decision January 15. The admission page does not state cycle years. Special arts awards can have additional requirements.
apply: Automatic general merit consideration with a complete Common Application or Coalition Application, personal essay, school report/counselor recommendation, official transcript, and at least one core-subject teacher evaluation. SAT/ACT are optional. Arts scholarships require additional materials.
eligibility: All admission applicants are automatically considered for general merit regardless of financial aid eligibility. Some named scholarships restrict location, school, STEM field, talent, or financial need. No general entry GPA floor is published; donor-specific renewal rules may differ.
notes: The Fall 2027 Denison Commitment is income-based tuition pricing and does not stack on top of merit. Merit can help fulfill that commitment, with the lower tuition outcome used. Merit amounts are guaranteed four years despite changes in family income; need-based aid is reevaluated.

name: General merit (Trustee unconfirmed)
value: The 2027–28 table lists Founders up to $18,000, Deans up to $16,000, Heritage up to $12,000, and Emeritus up to $8,000; payment frequency is not stated in the table. Merit scholarships are renewable for up to four years and fixed under the Hiram Guarantee. Global Scholarship for international students is up to $18,000 and cannot combine with other merit. Historical Trustee coverage is not confirmed.
deadline: Scholarship and aid applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. No separate merit application is required; no fixed merit deadline is published on the current page.
apply: Apply and gain admission to Hiram for automatic holistic merit consideration. The scholarship page instructs FAFSA submission for the aid package, but gives conflicting October 1 and December 1 opening dates; use the current federal form’s actual availability. Award notification follows admission.
eligibility: Merit review considers academic excellence, extracurricular distinction, motivation, and character. The 2027–28 table describes typical GPA profiles: Founders 4.0+, Deans 3.25–3.99, Heritage 2.75–3.24, Emeritus below 2.74; weighting is not stated and these are typical credentials rather than guaranteed thresholds. International students receive a separate holistic Global Scholarship review.
notes: The guarantee applies to tuition and merit award stability for on-campus undergraduate students; room, meals, fees, and other costs can change. Renewal depends on the particular award’s stipulations, which are not published numerically. The current page omits GPA 2.74 from its typical-profile ranges, so confirm that edge case rather than infer a tier.

name: Nonresident merit scholarships
value: Fall 2027 domestic nonresident annual awards by weighted GPA: 3.50–3.74 $8,000; 3.75–3.94 $14,000; 3.95–4.29 $15,000; 4.30+ $22,000. Renewable up to four years/eight semesters, usually fall and spring only. The required renewal GPA is specified in each financial aid offer and is reviewed after spring; it is not published numerically for these awards here.
deadline: Complete admission application, including transcript and recommendation, by the December 1, 2026 priority deadline for Fall 2027 merit consideration. Later consideration depends on availability.
apply: Automatic consideration with a complete admission application by the priority deadline; no separate general merit application. SAT/ACT are optional for general merit. Honors and Presidential Fellows applicants must opt in and report test scores for Fall 2027 consideration.
eligibility: Qualified domestic first-year students enrolling full-time at the Oxford campus in fall. Miami uses weighted GPA on a 4.0 scale from the transcript and recalculates it with course-difficulty weighting when the school does not provide one. Awards are not guaranteed. International students use the separate international scholarship rules.
notes: Full award generally requires at least 12 undergraduate credits; reduced enrollment requires approved appeal and proration. Changing to a regional campus forfeits the Oxford award for those semesters. Internships/co-ops without full-time tuition do not use an award semester; graduation and additional aid can affect eligibility. Prodesse for selected Honors students is separate from this domestic GPA table.

name: Presidential Fellows
value: Tuition and covered fees, standard double-occupancy housing, and Diplomat Standard meal plan for eight fall/spring semesters, renewable with a 3.50 cumulative GPA each year. Fifteen scholars annually. Includes a one-time enrichment fund up to $5,000 over four years, accessed through approved activity applications; unused funds are not refunded.
deadline: All admission, Honors/Presidential Fellows opt-in, and required self-reported SAT/ACT materials: December 1, 2026 for Fall 2027. Semifinalists complete a further application step after that deadline; finalists interview on campus in February 2027. Selection follows within two weeks of the interviews. Exact invitation instructions are sent to selected applicants.
apply: Indicate Honors College and Presidential Fellows interest on the admission application and provide all required materials, including self-reported SAT/ACT, by December 1. Selected semifinalists submit requested supplemental materials, then finalists take part in an invitation-only campus interview experience. No initial separate scholarship application is required.
eligibility: Top first-year Honors College applicants entering the Oxford campus in fall, including international applicants. For Fall 2027, self-reported SAT or ACT is required; no numerical PFP entry GPA or score floor is published. Maintain full-time Oxford enrollment and 3.50 cumulative GPA for renewal.
notes: Coverage excludes summer/winter terms, books, computers, supplies, health insurance, orientation, deposits, and optional charges. Housing and food upgrades cost extra; approved off-campus housing in years three/four is supported only up to standard costs and requires a university meal plan for food coverage. Approved Miami-billed study abroad can use the award for one fall/spring semester, with limited year-program exceptions. Additional aid can reduce the package to cost of attendance.

name: Mathile Scholarship
value: Full tuition for two entering students, renewable for a maximum of four years. Replaces all other ONU scholarships and awards. Specific renewal GPA and credit requirements are not stated on these pages.
deadline: Invited application, essay, and resume: end of day January 4, 2027, with no time zone stated. Finalist notification by January 15, 2027; interviews January 18–29, 2027; recipient notice by February 8, 2027.
apply: Admissions selects and invites applicants based on academic credentials; do not apply without an invitation. Submit a resume and leadership/community-service essay of approximately 500 words, maximum 750, as PDF or Word. Selected finalists complete an on-campus interview.
eligibility: Entering students with at least a 3.5 high school GPA, weighting unspecified, AND ACT 30 or SAT 1360 using evidence-based reading/writing plus math. The specific current page does not state a citizenship or major restriction.
notes: Full tuition does not establish room, meals, fees, or book coverage. Confirm award-specific academic renewal conditions in the offer.

name: James F. Dicke Scholarship
value: Full tuition plus a $1,000 annual book stipend for one recipient, renewable for a maximum of four years. Replaces all other ONU scholarships and awards. Specific renewal GPA and credit requirements are not stated on the public pages reviewed.
deadline: Application/registration with essay and resume: January 25, 2027. Required Dicke Scholarship Interview Day: January 30, 2027. No submission time or time zone is stated.
apply: Eligible students apply using the Dicke scholarship form, uploading a high school activities/work/leadership resume and an essay about ethical, analytical, and global leadership. Attend the January 30 interview day with faculty/student presentations. The current portal permits eligible applicants and does not require a prior admission invitation.
eligibility: Admitted to the Dicke College of Business Administration or declaring a major in that college, with cumulative high school GPA at least 3.5, weighting unspecified, AND ACT 27 or SAT 1260 using evidence-based reading/writing plus math. No separate citizenship restriction is stated on these pages.
notes: Corrected the source from the unrelated Mathile portal to the Dicke portal. The scholarship does not establish housing or meal coverage.

name: Stamps Eminence
value: Full cost of attendance for up to eight full-time semesters, plus enrichment grant funding up to $5,000. Renewal GPA is 3.4 or 3.5 depending on the academic program, without rounding, reviewed after the first year and annually thereafter; Honors status and active program participation are required.
deadline: Ohio State Early Action admission: November 1, 2026. Stamps Eminence essay/video application: November 9, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EST as stated by the program. Virtual finalist interviews January–February 2027; mandatory on-campus Finalist Friday February 26, 2027 in Columbus, with no attendance exceptions.
apply: Apply to Ohio State and indicate University Honors or Scholars interest; allow one to five days to receive and activate the OSU username. Submit the separate Eminence application using those credentials without waiting for an admission decision. Include a maximum 500-word problem-solving essay and a two-minute video via an unlisted, not private, YouTube link. Complete virtual finalist interview and required campus event if selected.
eligibility: New first-year students entering Ohio State Columbus in Autumn 2027, pursuing their first undergraduate degree. U.S. citizens and permanent residents are eligible; all majors encouraged. Must gain and maintain Honors status each semester, complete an Honors thesis or other capstone, engage in community service, and participate in required Eminence events. Entry academic selection is holistic; no numerical high school GPA cutoff is stated.
notes: Honors requires at least 18 hours of honors-quality coursework. The 3.5 college GPA rule applies to architecture, biomedical science, business, dental hygiene, education/human ecology, integrated business/engineering, and pharmacy; other programs generally use 3.4. Applying initially to Scholars is allowed, but Eminence finalists move into Honors.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: $28,000 annually for four years plus a one-time $3,000 experiential learning stipend. Maximum eight semesters within five consecutive calendar years or completion of a bachelor’s degree, whichever comes first. Renewal requires cumulative GPA at least 2.0, successful completion of at least 67% of attempted credits each semester, and degree completion within the published 150% timeframe.
deadline: November 1, 2026 (admission AND scholarship application)
apply: Create the admission application account, then submit the separate Presidential application using the same login. Upload an extracurricular resume, a personal essay up to 300 words, three additional essays up to 300 words each, and sign the integrity/release statement. The scholarship application also applies to Jesup Scott Honors College.
eligibility: Incoming freshmen with minimum cumulative high school GPA 3.8, weighting unspecified, who are U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens. Submit the complete admission application and documents by November 1, 2026, with official transcripts postmarked by that date. Full-time attendance is required each award semester.
notes: Half the annual award applies each fall and spring toward tuition/general fees up to 18 credits, campus housing, and meals. Replaces previous university scholarships; overlapping restricted aid or athletic awards may reduce or rescind it. Generally nonrefundable except approved institutional expenses. Co-op/internship requirements can be adjusted. Renewal reviewed after spring; failed renewal can be appealed for documented circumstances.

name: Barbara Hirschi Neely Scholarship
value: Five full-tuition awards for four years/eight semesters, plus a $2,000 project stipend available after the fourth semester and before graduation with faculty/program approval. Renewal requires full-time enrollment, good academic standing, cumulative GPA at least 2.0, at least 67% cumulative credit completion, and no more than 150% of program credits attempted; SAP is reviewed each semester.
deadline: Apply using Early Action or Early Decision. Published admission deadlines: Early Action/Early Decision I November 1 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific; Early Decision II January 15 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific. Cycle years and the Neely campus program/interview date are not stated on these pages; confirm Fall 2027 eligibility for the chosen round.
apply: Submit Common App admission, personal statement, transcript/secondary school report, and academic teacher recommendation using an eligible early admission round. Selected candidates participate in the day-long campus program and group interview; no separate initial Neely application is listed.
eligibility: High schools in Oregon counties Benton, Clackamas, Clatsop, Columbia, Hood River, Lincoln, Linn, Marion, Multnomah, Polk, Tillamook, Washington or Yamhill, or Clark County, Washington.
notes: Eligibility depends on the location of the high school, rather than merely residence in Oregon or Washington. Other merit awards such as Sequoia and Oregon Maple are separate. The college now uses test-free admission, so SAT/ACT are not considered for general admission.

name: Distinguished / Presidential Distinguished merit
value: First-year Distinguished/Presidential Distinguished awards up to $34,000 annually for 2027–28, tuition only; transfer awards up to $27,000 annually. Undergraduate merit is available for up to four years of full-time enrollment. Renewal requires successful completion of 24 credits per academic year and cumulative GPA at least 1.75 after the first year and 2.0 for upper-class students, plus good academic standing.
deadline: Admission and scholarship offers are rolling. January 15 is the priority deadline for automatic Distinguished scholarship consideration; its cycle year is not stated. No separate merit application is required.
apply: Apply for admission through Common App or Arcadia App and submit the high school transcript or self-reported grades; official transcript is required after admission and deposit. Ordinary first-year personal essay, activities, recommendations, and SAT/ACT are optional; special admission routes have additional requirements. Merit consideration is automatic after admission.
eligibility: First-year award review uses high school academic performance and school/community involvement; transfer review uses cumulative GPA and coursework. No numerical general entry GPA floor is stated. Full-time undergraduate enrollment required. International applicants use Common App and follow the international admission/testing requirements.
notes: Merit is tuition-specific and can be replaced or reduced when other awards cover tuition. FAFSA is used for federal and need-based grants; the merit policy does not require it. The historical full-tuition President’s award is not confirmed by the current $34,000 listing.

name: Rees-Chancellor's Scholars
value: Full tuition, room and board, plus guaranteed funding for study abroad, internships, and research. Award duration, experiential funding limits, and renewal GPA/credit requirements are not published on the checked pages.
deadline: December 1, 2026 priority for complete Pitt and Frederick Honors College materials, based on Pitt's August 2026 announcement of the open admission cycle. Semifinalist and finalist interviews follow by invitation; confirm portal instructions.
apply: Apply to Pitt, indicate Frederick Honors College interest, submit all required materials, and be accepted into Frederick Honors College. Selected semifinalists and finalists complete two interview rounds.
eligibility: Incoming undergraduate students described by the program as U.S. residents or DACA recipients. Review considers weighted GPA, curriculum, optional applicable tests/rank, activities, and Common App essay or Pitt personal statement. Research and leadership experience are recommended. The page does not define U.S. residents as a citizenship category.
notes: Pitt's August 2026 news confirms an existing 2026 cohort, while the program page still says its first cohort will enter Fall 2027. Benefits are defined, but award duration, experiential funding limits, renewal terms, and the scope of “U.S. residents” are not published.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: 25 annual awards covering undergraduate fall/spring tuition, campus housing, a meal plan up to 21 meals weekly, the general fee, and Textbook Access Program fee. Maximum one undergraduate degree or eight semesters. Annual renewal requires overall GPA at least 3.33, program obligations, and director approval; the published probation process allows three semesters to restore GPA after probation begins.
deadline: For the 2026-27 admission campaign (Fall 2027 entry), submit Villanova admission by January 15, 2027 for automatic initial Presidential Scholarship consideration. Selected candidates receive supplemental deadlines in the applicant portal and may be invited to a required on-campus interview.
apply: Apply for admission by the scholarship cutoff. Selected candidates receive admission-portal invitations for short-answer/essay materials, then finalists must attend the multi-day campus interview. No nomination is required since September 2024, and nomination letters are not accepted. FAFSA/CSS are not required for scholarship consideration.
eligibility: First-time first-year undergraduate applicants, including international students; transfers are excluded. No GPA or SAT/ACT minimum is published. SAT/ACT are optional for the explicitly stated 2026–27 admission campaign, Class of 2031. International admission is need-aware, and ability to pay can affect admission and eligibility for the scholarship.
notes: Current Villanova FAQ identifies the 2026-27 admission campaign as Class of 2031, confirms the January 15 initial consideration date, and says later invitation deadlines are supplied individually in the portal. Follow portal notices for the supplemental application and interview.

name: Academic merit
value: Academic merit awards average about $25,000 annually and renew for four years subject to academic standards. Separately, one Roddy award can cover tuition, fees, housing and food for an entering student planning medical, dental, or optometry graduate study; Roddy renewal criteria must be obtained from the college.
deadline: Published admission deadlines: Early Action/Early Decision I November 1; Regular Decision/Early Decision II January 15. Supporting credentials are due at least 10 days after the application deadline. Cycle years are not stated. First-year merit consideration is automatic.
apply: Submit Common App, the required personal statement/Common App essay, secondary school report/high school transcript, and application fee or waiver. The supplemental essay and SAT/ACT are optional. General academic merit and Roddy require no separate application; merit-only consideration or renewal does not require FAFSA/CSS.
eligibility: First-year academic merit is based on academic achievement; the typical 3.8 recalculated unweighted GPA is a recipient profile, not a guaranteed threshold. Roddy recipients must reside in the U.S. and plan the specified graduate professional study. Separate fine arts, service-major, Cristo Rey, and transfer programs have different rules.
notes: This listing covers Providence first-year academic merit and the distinct Roddy award. Named academic scholarships have published full-time and GPA standards; Roddy's separate renewal standards are not published. The earlier blanket Honors full-tuition claim is not confirmed.

name: National Scholars
value: Cost of attendance, including tuition, fees, housing, food, and other expenses, plus educational enrichment and study/travel abroad. As a first-year recruiting scholarship, the general published limit is four years/eight semesters with cumulative Clemson GPA at least 3.0 and 24 earned credits annually; more specific award conditions are supplied in iROAR.
deadline: For the Fall 2027 selection process, apply Early Action by October 15, 2026 and Honors Priority by October 22, 2026; required admission and Honors materials by November 1, 2026. The explicitly labeled 2027 cohort interview weekend is February 19–20, 2027, with January invitations and early March decisions. Time zones are not stated.
apply: Submit Clemson undergraduate Early Action and the separate Honors Priority application, including two essays, activities, awards, STARS academic record and two recommendations by the published deadlines. Selected finalists must attend the February 19–20, 2027 recruitment weekend. Clemson’s broader Named Scholarship page also says to file the FAFSA by January 1 for named-program consideration, while the specific National Scholars page lists only the two applications and includes international applicants; check how the FAFSA instruction applies to this program.
eligibility: New first-year applicants in all residency categories, explicitly including international students. No entry GPA or score floor is published. Selection assesses academics, intellectual curiosity, leadership and community impact; this is separate from National Merit.
notes: Clemson's current first-year admissions and counselor pages state a test-optional policy without the Honors page's older 2026–27 qualifier. The specific National Scholars page admits applicants regardless of residency, including international students. Its application list conflicts with the general Named Scholarship page's FAFSA statement; international applicants cannot use federal FAFSA. General first-year recruiting renewal is 3.0 cumulative GPA and 24 earned credits annually; award-specific conditions accompany iROAR offers. Optional supplemental materials are not required.

name: James B. Duke Scholarship
value: Full tuition, room, board, and all fees for four years/eight semesters. Renewal requires cumulative GPA at least 3.00 at the end of each academic year. Includes Riley Institute Advantage Scholars and Community of Scholars programming.
deadline: November 1 priority deadline for premier scholarships; selected candidates receive early February invitations for a March interview event. The cycle year and exact interview dates are not stated.
apply: Initial consideration uses the admission application with no separate initial Duke scholarship form. Selected finalists are invited to interview in March and notified by mail. Duke replaces any previously offered Bell Tower award.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students with exceptional academics, leadership, service, and co-curricular involvement. Typical top 1–2% applicant ranking and ACT above 34/SAT above 1500 describe past finalists, not published mandatory thresholds. General admission is test optional; no separate Duke nationality or state restriction is stated.
notes: Other premier scholarships have distinct geographic rules. The renewal policy still names the historical Lay award, but the current merit directory does not confirm a separate Lay award accepting new applicants.

name: Wofford Scholars
value: Award family totaling $60,000–$250,000 over four years: 1854 awards $15,000–$25,000 annually; Benjamin Wofford $27,000–$30,000 annually; two Daniel awards cover tuition, fees, food and housing. Richardson provides four-year tuition, fees, room/board, a monthly book/personal stipend, laptop, summer internships, and January travel. Renewal requirements are supplied in the individual award letter.
deadline: 2027 graduates: nomination/self-nomination by November 6, 2026; admission Early Decision November 1, 2026 or Early Action November 15, 2026, with all materials by the corresponding deadline. Scholars Day interview November 14, 2026, or an approved alternate Scholars Day as stated on the self-nomination form. No cutoff time is published.
apply: Obtain a high school counselor nomination or self-nominate, then submit Common App using an eligible early round, counselor secondary school report, and official transcript. Recommendations are encouraged, not required. Attend Scholars Day group interview or approved alternate. Richardson finalists have an additional interview, and the Richardson page specifically requires a counselor nomination.
eligibility: Prospective first-year students with top 10% class standing and at least 1300 SAT/PSAT or 28 ACT/PLAN, plus leadership/service. If the school does not rank, the self-nomination form says transcripts may be requested. No specific nationality/residency restriction is published for the general family.
notes: The listing covers distinct Wofford Scholars award levels; amounts and benefits depend on the selected award. Renewal follows the individual award letter. General Wofford Scholars permits self-nomination, but Richardson specifically requires a high-school counselor nomination. Older 2025-26 handbook GPA figures should not be projected onto a 2027 offer.

name: McNair Scholars
value: McNair: $24,000 annually plus tuition reduction to the in-state rate for four years/eight terms and a $14,000 enrichment fund. Renewal requires full-time Columbia enrollment, ordinarily 12 undergraduate credits each fall/spring, and cumulative USC system GPA at least 3.0, checked after spring.
deadline: Complete the separate Honors/Top Scholars application by November 15, 2026; all required credentials, including one recommendation, by December 1, 2026. Optional Early Action admission deadline October 15, 2026. Mandatory semifinalist virtual interviews in late January 2027, followed by finalist campus weekend February 27–March 1, 2027. No cutoff time or time zone is stated.
apply: Apply for undergraduate admission and indicate Honors interest; the separate Honors application appears in the portal after approximately 48 hours. Complete the admission essay/activities, two additional Honors essays, unofficial transcript, and one recommendation. A resume is optional. Semifinalists interview virtually and finalists attend Top Scholar Weekend.
eligibility: First-time first-year nonresident applicants admitted to a USC degree program; nonresidents must be lawfully present in the U.S. Eligibility is based on academic merit without a financial-need criterion. Published GPA/test/class-rank ranges are profiles, not mandatory floors. Tests are explicitly optional for Fall, Spring, and Summer 2027.
notes: Up to 20 nonresident McNair awards annually. Stamps and Horseshoe are separate Top Scholar awards with different values. Normally one General University Scholarship may be held, with named exceptions. Summer use counts toward the eight-term maximum; donor approval is required to use remaining McNair eligibility for graduate/professional study.

name: Oak Alley and institutional merit
value: Oak Alley full tuition; Cambridge $45,000 annually; Presidential $40,000; Founders and Ralph C. Hon $38,000; Diehl $36,000; Rhodes Award $20,000–$34,000. These automatic merit awards are renewable up to four years/eight semesters and cannot stack with each other. General institutional-aid SAP requires cumulative GPA at least 1.50 and 67% course completion after freshman year, then GPA at least 2.00 and 67% completion after sophomore year.
deadline: Published admission deadlines: Early Decision I November 1, Early Action November 15, Early Decision II/Regular Decision January 15. Early Decision has priority scholarship review. No cycle years are stated; no separate initial application is required for these named merit awards.
apply: Submit Common App, personal essay, official transcript, counselor secondary school report/recommendation, and at least one teacher recommendation; Regular Decision also requires a midyear report. SAT/ACT and the 90-second video are optional. Automatic named merit consideration requires no separate scholarship form.
eligibility: Admission applicants are assessed individually for academic talent, service, and leadership, without a published universal entry GPA threshold. International applicants are explicitly eligible for merit from $20,000 annually to full tuition; additional English proficiency and a non-U.S.-citizen financial-information form apply to their admission route.
notes: Full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits is required, including the final senior semester. Awards cover fall/spring only and ordinary 12–18-credit loads; overload costs are extra. Rhodes-funded gift aid cannot exceed direct costs and other aid can cause reductions. Interest/affinity awards use separate applications and eligibility, so this award family should be split. An older Bellingrath award is not confirmed in the current directory.

name: Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship
value: Full tuition for up to four undergraduate years, renewed annually with GPA at least 3.0, plus a one-time summer stipend after sophomore or junior year for an immersive experience. The stipend amount is not stated. Additional need-based aid may cover demonstrated need beyond tuition.
deadline: Scholarship materials due December 1, 2026; recipients notified at the end of March 2027. Admission must be submitted first to obtain MyAppVU, ordinarily in 2–3 business days. No cutoff time or time zone is stated.
apply: Submit admission through Common App, Coalition, or QuestBridge, then upload the scholarship response as PDF or Word in MyAppVU. The application is strongly encouraged and preference goes to applicants. The Fall 2027 response is 250–500 words addressing the chosen academic program; use the first-choice school if applying to more than one. Confirm submission date/green check; post-submission corrections are not accepted.
eligibility: Entering first-year undergraduate students, including international applicants; transfers are excluded. Selection uses academic achievement, intellectual promise, leadership and contributions outside class. Tests are optional for Fall 2027; no entry GPA/score floor or required major is published. Blair audition results affect merit selection.
notes: Financial need is not a selection factor and no need-based aid application is required for merit consideration. Early Decision provides no selection advantage, but its commitment comes before late-March merit notification.

name: Ingram Scholarship
value: Full tuition, required fees, and the value of on-campus housing each year through senior year, plus a special summer-service-project stipend of unpublished amount. Annual renewal requires GPA at least 3.0 and fulfillment of service obligations. Additional need-based aid may cover demonstrated need beyond tuition.
deadline: Prospective first-year scholarship applications: December 1, 2026; selected finalists must interview and merit notification is in late March 2027. For currently enrolled first-year students, applications open mid-January 2027 and applications/reference letters are due February 28, 2027, with notification in the second half of May 2027. Exact finalist interview dates are not stated.
apply: Submit admission first, then upload scholarship responses in MyAppVU as PDF or Word. Application is strongly encouraged with applicant preference. The Fall 2027 first-year document requires three responses of 250–500 words each. Selected finalists interview with the committee. Current-first-year applicants use the separate spring route and reference letters.
eligibility: Entering first-year students, including international applicants, and a limited separate route for currently enrolled first-year students. Transfers are ineligible for entering-first-year merit. Tests are optional for Fall 2027; no entry GPA/score floor or required major is published. Selection emphasizes civic service, entrepreneurship, character, and leadership.
notes: Scholars must serve 20 hours monthly during the academic year, complete a summer service project after sophomore year, and attend weekly small/large-group meetings. Financial need is not a selection factor; no need-based aid forms are required for merit consideration.

name: Murchison; Trinity Tower/Semmes
value: Murchison $18,000–$30,000 annually; Tower and Semmes full tuition. Semmes also includes a $5,000 research/travel/materials stipend. All three renew up to eight semesters with full-time enrollment and SAP; Tower/Semmes additionally require cumulative GPA at least 3.0, reviewed annually. Tower/Semmes replace other institutional grants/scholarships and fund fall/spring tuition only.
deadline: Murchison admission cutoff February 1, cycle year unstated. Tower requires Early Decision I/Early Action admission by November 1, with a spring competition whose exact 2027 date is not stated. Semmes: admission November 1, 2026, separate scholarship application November 8, 2026, and finalist campus interview February 6, 2027. No cutoff time is stated.
apply: Admission automatically considers Murchison and Tower; Tower finalists are invited to Scholars Day competition. Semmes requires a separate scholarship application and expanded resume, followed by selected finalist campus interviews. SAT/ACT are optional on all three specific scholarship pages.
eligibility: Entering first-year undergraduates; transfer, continuing, and graduate students excluded. Murchison expects at least 3.5 core GPA recalculated unweighted, rather than a guarantee. Semmes requires planned biology, biochemistry, biochemistry/molecular biology, chemistry, computer science, engineering science, geosciences, mathematics, neuroscience, physics/astronomy, or psychology study. No universal GPA floor applies to this grouped family.
notes: This directory groups Murchison, Trinity Tower and Semmes, which have distinct awards and routes. Semmes publishes 2027 dates. Tower's official page itself says both up to 25 and up to 20 full-tuition awards; no single count is claimed here. Murchison and Tower cycle years remain unconfirmed.

name: Forty Acres Scholars
value: Four-year program covering full tuition and providing living, book/supply, and enrichment stipends. The sponsor does not state fixed stipend amounts; enrichment funds support approved experiences.
deadline: Fall 2027: final admission application December 1, 2026, supporting admission materials and official tests December 10, 2026. Optional Early Action October 15, 2026 with supporting materials October 22, 2026. Optional scholarship-interest form, expanded resume and essay due January 15, 2027. Semifinalists receive additional instructions; exact scholarship interview/weekend dates are unpublished.
apply: Apply for UT Austin admission for automatic initial consideration. Submit required admission essay/short answers, transcripts, official SAT/ACT or accepted CLT scores, and applicable major materials. The optional MyStatus Scholarship Interest Form adds an expanded resume/essay; no standalone initial scholarship application is required. Selected semifinalists complete additional materials/interviews and finalists participate in Finalist Weekend.
eligibility: High-school seniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent U.S. residents at application. Both Texas residents and out-of-state students are eligible; transfer and international students are not.
notes: Fall 2027 admission dates and U.S. citizen/permanent-resident eligibility are confirmed. Applying to UT Austin automatically gives scholarship consideration. The optional interest form in MyStatus requests an expanded résumé and essay; additional selection instructions are sent to chosen applicants.

name: Eugene McDermott Scholars
value: Eleven semesters over four years, including summers: UT Dallas tuition/mandatory fees, housing and living stipends, and up to $15,000 study-abroad/engagement funding. Approximate published value $180,000 for Texas students or $310,000 for non-Texas students. Semester and cumulative GPA and engagement-hour standards apply, but numerical requirements are unpublished.
deadline: Fall 2027 UT Dallas admission opens August 1, 2026; complete admission by December 1, 2026 for AES review, a McDermott prerequisite. The separate McDermott Scholarship application deadline for the entering class of 2027 has not been published. Do not use the prior-cycle dates still shown on its pages.
apply: Apply to UT Dallas first for the NetID, earn an AES offer, and submit the separate McDermott application with two completed McDermott recommendation forms. Finalists must attend a virtual event and complete asynchronous VidCruiter interviews. Scholarship reviewers see the McDermott application/forms rather than admission grades or tests. FAFSA is not required.
eligibility: Domestic and international first-time first-year applicants in any major who enter in fall immediately after high-school graduation, without a gap year or transfer. McDermott requires an AES offer and top-academic-tenth standing; the official program page still labels the entering class of 2026, so confirm 2027 criteria when published.
notes: The McDermott official page still describes the 2026 cohort and its 2026 event dates. UT Dallas has published Fall 2027 admission opening and December 1, 2026 AES review, but not the separate 2027 McDermott deadline. Its approximate award valuation is published without a specified cohort and may change.

name: Academic Excellence Scholarship (AES)
value: Competitive amounts vary by entering cohort and can reach or exceed full tuition; Fall 2027 award tiers are unpublished. Maximum eight funded semesters. Renewal requires semester GPA at least 3.0, cumulative GPA at least 3.0 at each academic year’s end, full-time enrollment ordinarily 12 undergraduate credits, conduct compliance, and degree-credit pacing toward four-year graduation.
deadline: For Fall 2027, complete the UT Dallas admission file by December 1, 2026 for automatic AES consideration. Award acceptance is due June 1 on the AES page, but its cycle year is not explicit; verify the offer notice.
apply: Submit Common App or ApplyTexas, official high school transcripts, and the fee or waiver. No separate AES application is required. Essay, resume, and up to three recommendations are encouraged but optional. The main admission page explicitly does not require tests for scholarship consideration; the AES page’s eligibility list mentions scores but elsewhere says scores are considered if available, so confirm the current policy.
eligibility: Domestic and international first-time-in-college freshmen entering fall immediately after high school graduation; no specific GPA, rank, or test result guarantees an award. All AES recipients qualify for resident tuition/fee charges regardless of residency. Maintain four-year degree pacing, ordinarily 15 credits per semester/30 annually; applicable AP, IB and dual credit can count toward pacing.
notes: The Fall 2027 admission page and AES page establish December 1, 2026 automatic review. Both allow review without SAT/ACT scores; an AES checklist initially mentions scores but explicitly gives a no-score option. Award tiers for the entering class of 2027 are not published.

name: President's Scholars
value: Full tuition and general fees for eight consecutive fall/spring semesters or graduation; approved study-abroad tuition and round-trip airfare. A separate Campus Community Award covers eligible on-campus housing and specified meal plans while engagement conditions are met.
deadline: Admission November 1; scholarship essay November 16, 11:59 p.m. CST; finalist interviews first Friday in March. Fall 2027 cycle years and interview date are not explicitly published.
apply: Submit the admission application first, then the separate President’s Scholars essay in the admission portal, maximum three double-spaced pages. SAT or ACT scores are required for this scholarship. Complete all admission materials and any Meadows dual-admit audition/portfolio requirements in the fall. Selected finalists must interview on campus. FAFSA and CSS Profile are not required for merit consideration.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students with rigorous academic preparation, including 20 academic units, two years of the same foreign language, and advanced mathematics/science. Top-ten-percent standing is expected; students at schools without rank may demonstrate a strong record. Published score and GPA profiles are competitive descriptions, not guaranteed selection thresholds.
notes: Renewal requires 3.300 cumulative GPA and full-time enrollment of at least 12 hours. Campus Community housing/meal support has separate eligible residence, meal-plan, and engagement rules. Study-abroad room/board, deposits, books, insurance, parking, and special course fees are not covered by the core scholarship. Standard summer and January terms are not included.

name: Brown Scholarship
value: $48,000 per year, renewable annually for up to eight semesters while maintaining Southwestern satisfactory academic progress. Any additional individual offer terms should be checked in the award letter.
deadline: Admission and merit application by the first Tuesday in December; required Brown interview by the first Tuesday in February. Fall 2027 cycle years are not explicitly published.
apply: The admission application also serves as the merit application. Submit the required application essay, school recommendation or accepted secondary-school report, and official high-school transcript. Complete the Brown interview by the published recurring deadline; a campus visit and letter of interest are encouraged.
eligibility: Top 5% class rank, or at least 3.8 unweighted GPA if the school does not rank. Financial need is not a factor in academic merit selection.
notes: Southwestern's current general scholarship policy covers Brown renewal under its eight-semester SAP rule and lists Brown in the stacking rules. No Brown-specific numeric GPA condition is stated. Application and interview deadlines are given as first Tuesdays in December and February without a current cycle year.

name: Chancellor's Scholarship
value: Full tuition for eight first-year semesters, or six semesters for selected transfers. A 2026–27 aid table lists fees too, but the Fall 2027 admissions description only confirms tuition; verify fees in the offer.
deadline: Fall 2027 first-year applicants: admission November 1, 2026; Honors application November 15, 2026. Invitations by January 15, 2027; Chancellor’s experience February 14–16, 2027, including February 16 interviews. Transfer dates are published without explicit cycle years.
apply: First-year applicants should complete the admission application, required 250–650-word essay, transcript, counselor and teacher recommendations, and the Honors application with one essay up to 800 words. Selected finalists attend two interviews. U.S.-residing finalists are expected in person; finalists residing internationally may request video interviews. Transfer candidates complete the separate transfer scholarship process and materials.
eligibility: First-year selection considers exceptional academic performance, leadership, service, and writing. Test scores are not considered in Chancellor’s selection. Transfer candidates require a 3.85 cumulative GPA and 60 transferable hours by enrollment; AP credit does not count toward this minimum, but dual-enrollment credit can.
notes: Current first-year Chancellor page explicitly dates the Fall 2027 selection event. Its award description confirms tuition; the aid office's older 2026–27 grid includes fees, so fee inclusion for the 2027 offer is unconfirmed. Transfer applicants have a published separate route but its next-cycle cutoff years are not specified.

name: Tier One Scholars
value: Tuition and mandatory fees for four years, or five years for architecture; eligible housing and meal support for the first two years; one-time $1,000 research and $2,000 study-abroad stipends. Eligible nonresidents receive a tuition waiver.
deadline: Fall 2027: complete admission and Tier One application by November 2, 2026, 5 p.m. Central; recommender letter November 9, 2026, 5 p.m. Central. Interview invitations December 4, 2026; virtual interviews December 16, 17, or 18, 2026.
apply: Complete admission first and obtain the UH ID, normally emailed within four business days, then submit the separate Tier One application. Name a recommender who uploads the letter directly by the recommendation deadline. Selected finalists complete a virtual interview. FAFSA is encouraged, not required for this merit award.
eligibility: Incoming Fall 2027 freshmen; transfer, graduate, and continuing UH students are excluded. Test-optional candidates are considered. Published 1400 SAT/30 ACT/top-10% and recipient GPA profiles are not hard floors.
notes: Renewal requires at least 12 hours each fall/spring and 3.0 cumulative UH GPA. Degree-applicable credits must reach 30, 60, and 90 by the ends of the first three summers; eligible AP, dual, and transfer credits can count. Summer credits/GPA can help renewal, but summer tuition is not funded. Tier One replaces Academic Excellence funding rather than stacking with it.

name: President's Endowed (National Scholar component)
value: $3,000 per year for four years ($12,000 total), plus a one-time $1,000 education-abroad award, as the President’s Endowed component of an eligible National Scholar package.
deadline: Scholarship sections and STARS record due December 1. Fall 2027 cycle year and National Merit designation stages are not explicitly published here.
apply: Apply for fall freshman admission to College Station using Common App or ApplyTexas, complete both admission and scholarship sections, and submit STARS by the scholarship deadline. Admission requires the essay and short-answer questions; ApplyTexas applicants also complete the extracurricular activities form. National Merit Finalists seeking the separate Recognition award must designate Texas A&M as first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: Fall-entering College Station freshmen who are National Merit Semifinalists or Finalists are guaranteed the listed President’s Endowed component under the current National Scholars page. Other President’s Endowed competitive routes are separate.
notes: This $3,000 annual component alone does not satisfy the published $4,000 eligible-scholarship threshold for a nonresident tuition waiver. National Merit Finalists may receive distinct $7,000 annual Recognition and $500 annual Sponsorship components under their own rules. Current numeric renewal conditions are not established; a 2018 university article reported a 3.5 GPA requirement, which is historical evidence only.

name: President John R. Park Scholarship
value: Fall 2027 (2027–28) terms are marked Coming Soon. Historical Fall 2026 award: $10,000 per academic year, renewable up to eight fall/spring semesters or first bachelor’s degree.
deadline: General first-year early-action/merit consideration deadline is December 1, without an explicit cycle year. Fall 2027 Park-specific dates are not published.
apply: Complete the university first-year application and official transcript requirements for merit consideration. Utah high-school graduates may use the Beehive Application or Common App; other applicants use Common App. Test scores are ordinarily optional, with requirements for homeschool, non-accredited U.S. schools, and GED/HiSET applicants. Fall 2027 Park-specific application terms remain unpublished.
eligibility: Current program description covers first-time first-year Utah residents and nonresidents from states outside the WUE-eligible group. The historical 2026–27 4.00 unweighted entry GPA is not confirmed for Fall 2027.
notes: Historical 2026–27 terms specified tuition/mandatory-fee coverage up to award amount, no housing supplement or course/program fees, 12 completed credits each term, 24 annually and 3.50 cumulative GPA; nonstacking with most university merit and main-campus restrictions applied. These prior-cycle terms do not establish Fall 2027 renewal or award rules.

name: Richmond Scholars
value: 25 awards covering full tuition, housing, and food for up to eight consecutive full-time semesters; eligibility for a one-time faculty-mentored enrichment grant up to $5,500.
deadline: For Fall 2027, submit admission by December 1, 2026 for automatic Richmond Scholars consideration. Finalists are notified in their portal and invited to an interview; the exact 2027 interview schedule is supplied to finalists.
apply: Apply for admission through Common App or Coalition App, including the required Richmond essay (350–650 words), transcript, and school-official recommendation. No separate initial scholarship application. Submit supporting credentials by the admission-plan deadline. Selected finalists complete a faculty Zoom interview. International applicants must submit the Certification of Financial Responsibility for admission.
eligibility: Incoming first-year applicants, including international students and non-U.S. citizens. Fall 2027 applicants may apply without SAT/ACT scores. Selection considers academic achievement, engaged leadership, purpose, and contribution to a diverse community; no numeric entry GPA floor is published.
notes: The current program page confirms 25 awards covering tuition, housing, and food for up to eight full-time semesters. The up-to-$5,500 enrichment grant needs a separate approved project application. Selection-page test-language naming entrants in 2024 is stale; Fall 2027 test policy comes from current admissions materials.

name: Jefferson Scholarship
value: Tuition, room, board, books, and miscellaneous expenses for four years/eight full-time semesters at UVA, plus supplemental enrichment experiences. Current additional renewal conditions are not publicly established.
deadline: Current foundation selection page lists December 1 for counselor and nominee materials; its cycle year is not explicit. Regional interviews follow in winter and final virtual interviews in late February by invitation. UVA admission is separate: early admission November 1 and regular admission January 5, with supporting materials on the published UVA schedule.
apply: Obtain nomination from an eligible high school; students cannot self-apply. The counselor submits one recommendation, transcript, and school profile. The nominee submits activities, awards, a personal statement, and a leadership essay. Complete any regional interview and final virtual interview, and separately apply to and gain admission to UVA. UVA may also refer selected early applicants. UVA uses Common App and requires the secondary-school report, school profile, transcript, and one academic-subject teacher evaluation; a separate counselor recommendation is optional. Fall 2027 admission is test optional.
eligibility: High-school seniors selected for leadership, scholarship, and engaged citizenship. U.S. citizenship and financial need are not selection requirements; eligible schools outside the U.S. can nominate for Jefferson. Walentas is a distinct first-generation scholarship.
notes: The foundation defines four-year cost-of-attendance coverage plus enrichment, but current nomination cycle year is not explicitly printed on its public selection page. Exact finalist scheduling is supplied to nominees. Jefferson and first-generation Walentas are distinct awards.

name: Johnson Scholarship
value: Tuition and fees, housing and food, plus up to $10,000 total summer enhancement funding during enrollment; up to 44 incoming students, roughly 10% of the class. Additional demonstrated need may increase coverage. Current award duration and specific renewal conditions need confirmation.
deadline: Admission application and Johnson essay December 1, 2026, 11:59 p.m. in the applicant’s local time zone; supporting materials December 15, 2026. Finalist notice early February and campus selection event early March; exact Fall 2027 event dates are not published.
apply: Complete the admission application plus Johnson supplemental essay, maximum 800 words, regardless of admission plan. Required admission materials include transcript, two teacher recommendations, counselor recommendation, and secondary-school report; test scores are optional. QuestBridge Finalists are automatically considered when their application is forwarded and need not submit the Johnson essay. Selected finalists interview during an all-expenses-paid campus selection event.
eligibility: Incoming first-year applicants, including international applicants; selection considers academic achievement, leadership, integrity, and campus/civic contributions. Transfer applicants are not eligible under the published scholarship table. International admission requires English proficiency and applicable school-leaving results.
notes: W&L confirms award coverage and summer enhancement. Its detailed instructions retain an older Class of 2029 test reference and a January 1 QuestBridge non-finalist exception; use the current general December 1, 2026 route unless W&L confirms the exception for Fall 2027. Johnson-specific renewal terms are given in the award notice.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: 25 Presidential Program scholarships ranging from $33,000 per year to full tuition, renewable for four years; awards incorporate other Carthage assistance.
deadline: Admission, transcript, scholarship application, essay, and activities list December 3, 2026. Selected second round in January or February 2027; exact event dates are not published.
apply: Apply for admission and submit a high-school transcript, then the separate Presidential Scholarship application with a maximum 250-word essay and activities/work list. Selected candidates attend an on-campus or remote second round with two faculty/staff conversations and an additional essay. SAT/ACT scores and admission recommendation letters are optional.
eligibility: Incoming full-time undergraduates seeking their first bachelor’s degree; all majors may compete. Selection considers academic strength and leadership. No program entry GPA floor is published.
notes: The Presidential Program includes 25 named awards. Carthage's current aid table gives the Presidential award a 2.75 renewal GPA and several named awards a 3.25 GPA; consult the actual award notice for the applicable named condition. Second-round event invitations are sent individually, with exact dates not yet published.

name: School of Business and Economics Scholarship
value: Two full-tuition scholarships per year, renewable for four years; each incorporates other Carthage assistance and combined aid is capped at tuition.
