deadline: For Fall 2027, the current Carthage scholarship directory lists December 3 for admission and the Business scholarship application. The Business-specific page still shows December 3, 2025 and a February 6 second-round event from the previous cycle; a 2027 event date is not confirmed.
apply: Apply for admission with a high-school transcript and submit the separate Business and Economics scholarship application with a one-page essay about career interest. Selected finalists attend the on-campus or remote February event and take a comprehensive examination. Admission test scores and recommendation letters are optional.
eligibility: Incoming full-time freshmen seeking their first bachelor’s degree who intend to major in accounting, economics, finance, healthcare administration, human resources, management, or marketing. A double major in another subject is allowed.
notes: The current directory says its competitive scholarship amounts apply to students starting Fall 2027 or later and lists a December 3 Business application. The linked Business page still has Fall 2026 closure and 2025/2026 dates. Use the current application portal for cycle confirmation. Current public pages do not establish a Business-specific numeric renewal GPA; general SAP applies.

name: Karsh International Scholars
value: Tuition, room, board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need exceeding those costs, and three summers of research/internship funding. University merit guidance supports four years, subject to award-specific academic qualifications; summer funding limits and specific renewal conditions are not published.
deadline: Fall 2027 Duke Early Decision application and CSS Profile: November 2, 2026 on the current admission checklist; Regular Decision application January 4, 2027 and aid forms February 1, 2027. An older Duke financial-support page still says November 3 for ED aid, so verify the exact aid deadline in the applicant portal.
apply: Apply to Duke, select financial-aid interest, and submit the required CSS Profile and any requested income/tax documentation. No separate Karsh application. Admission requires the main application and essays, transcript, secondary-school report with counselor recommendation, and two teacher recommendations. SAT/ACT scores and admission interviews are optional. International aid applicants must follow their aid checklist.
eligibility: International first-year applicants with demonstrated financial need and strong academic/civic engagement. Citizens of countries outside the U.S. may be considered, but dual U.S./foreign citizens and applicants who already have a bachelor’s degree are excluded. International transfer students are not eligible for merit or need aid.
notes: Karsh requires international first-year applicants to request financial aid with Duke admission; there is no separate Karsh application. Current 2026-27 admission checklist says ED aid forms November 2, while an older aid page still says November 3. Summer funding is a defined benefit, but its dollar limit and Karsh-specific renewal conditions are not published.

name: Century Scholars
value: Two-year faculty research mentoring, a two-year merit scholarship, and a research stipend; dollar amounts are not published. Funding does not extend beyond sophomore year.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision I November 1, 2026; Early Decision II or Regular Decision January 4, 2027; Shepherd School of Music December 1, 2026. No separate Century application.
apply: All admitted freshmen are considered automatically. Complete admission application and Rice writing supplement, transcript, counselor and two teacher recommendations, and the required Rice Box image. International applicants also submit English-proficiency evidence as applicable and the International Student Financial Statement. Music and architecture applicants have additional audition/portfolio requirements. Tests and general admission interviews are optional.
eligibility: Selected incoming freshmen demonstrate strong academic/personal achievement or research enthusiasm. Prior research is not required. Scholars work with a faculty mentor for two years and must participate in Inquiry Weeks; sophomores present, while freshmen may present or volunteer.
notes: Rice's current program page defines a two-year merit scholarship, faculty mentoring and a research stipend for approved costs. The stipend amount is not published and is not an unrestricted cash award. It stops during study-abroad semesters; scholarship does not extend beyond sophomore year. Prior research is not required.

name: General merit (Trustee Distinguished unverified)
value: Rice confirms automatic freshman merit consideration, but does not publish a general award amount or duration here. The named Trustee Distinguished award and its current terms remain unconfirmed.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision I November 1, 2026; Early Decision II or Regular Decision January 4, 2027; Shepherd School of Music December 1, 2026. No separate Century application.
apply: All admitted freshmen are considered for general merit automatically; no separate form or merit interview is necessary. Complete admission application and Rice writing supplement, transcript, counselor and two teacher recommendations, and the required Rice Box image. International applicants also submit English-proficiency evidence as applicable and the International Student Financial Statement. Music and architecture applicants have additional audition/portfolio requirements. Tests and general admission interviews are optional.
eligibility: Incoming admitted freshman applicants are reviewed for exceptional academic and personal achievement. No universal entry GPA or citizenship restriction is stated for general merit consideration.
notes: Rice confirms automatic first-year merit consideration, but its current official aid page does not list a Trustee Distinguished award or publish a universal merit amount and renewal rule. Treat this listing as a general merit directory until a named award is confirmed.

name: Odyssey
value: Need-based access program.
notes: Not a merit award.

name: Chicago Public Schools Match (unverified)
value: Northwestern states its scholarships are not awarded on academic merit.

name: Automatic partial-tuition merit
value: Automatic partial-tuition merit up to $32,000 per year, ordinarily for four years; selected five-year undergraduate programs may receive five years.
deadline: Admission Early Decision I November 1; Early Action November 10; Early Decision II/Regular Decision January 15. Aid priority dates: November 15 for EDI, December 15 for EA, February 1 for EDII/RD. Current cycle years are not explicit.
apply: Complete Common App admission, personal statement and activities, school report/transcript, and counselor recommendation. No separate partial-merit scholarship form. Tulane expects CSS Profile and, for eligible U.S. applicants, FAFSA for merit consideration; international applicants submit CSS Profile and Declaration/Certification of Finances. Tests are optional but preferred for scholarship review.
eligibility: Entering first-year Newcomb-Tulane College students, including international applicants, selected on the strength of the admission application. No published entry GPA floor; separate full-tuition programs have different rules.
notes: Current June 2026 renewal policy requires full-time enrollment of 12 or more credits each fall/spring and generally 2.700 cumulative GPA for most other merit awards, unless the initial offer specifies otherwise. Review occurs each June; conduct/code violations or leave exceeding two years can terminate funding. Other Tulane resources may reduce/cancel merit; summer is not funded.

name: University Scholarship
value: University Scholarship amount is not published on the current program page. Institutional scholarships normally cover up to eight full-time fall/spring semesters or degree completion.
deadline: Admission Early Action/Early Decision I November 1; Early Decision II/Regular Decision January 15. Current cycle years are not explicit. February 15 belongs to separate scholarship competitions, not this automatic University Scholarship.
apply: Automatic consideration through admission. Submit Common App or Coalition with Scoir, required essay, official transcript, school report, counselor recommendation, and two teacher recommendations. SAT/ACT scores are optional. Aid forms are needed if also applying for need-based aid; no separate University Scholarship competition application is stated.
eligibility: First-year U.S. citizens and permanent residents meeting academic/personal scholarship selection criteria. This automatic-award citizenship restriction does not apply to every separate CWRU scholarship competition.
notes: Current 2026–27 Bulletin says scholarships renew with undergraduate status and continuous full-time enrollment, with eight-semester/degree cap and approved prorated final-semester option. Approved one-semester leave holds funding; reinstatement after longer leave is not guaranteed. Transfer to another institution/permanent separation ends funding. No numeric entry GPA floor or universal numeric renewal GPA is stated.

name: NYU Scholarship
value: University scholarship guidance describes awards based on academic achievement and, in most cases, demonstrated need. No single NYU Scholarship amount, duration, or universal renewal rule is established; merit-only awards are few.
deadline: Admission EDI November 1; EDII January 1; RD January 5, 11:59 p.m. applicant local time. CSS Profile EDI November 10; EDII January 10; RD February 1. Explicit current-cycle years are not published on these pages.
apply: Complete Common App, school report/transcript, one recommendation from a person in authority, and STARS after application. For institutional scholarship consideration submit CSS Profile, including required parent profiles or an approved waiver, by the aid deadline; eligible U.S. applicants also use FAFSA for federal aid. Submit required program audition/portfolio, English-proficiency evidence, and requested verification documents as applicable.
eligibility: First-time first-year applicants; scholarship selection and financial-aid rules vary by school/campus and award. U.S. and international first-year applicants use the appropriate aid pathway. Current general aid page excludes ordinary transfer/second-degree applicants from NYU scholarship funding; SPS DAUS has a separate process.
notes: This record describes a scholarship family, not a single verified merit-only award. Most scholarships renew automatically, with exceptions communicated by the aid office; the amount/conditions are award-specific. New York-campus NYU Promise is need-based and does not establish a merit award value. Campus and school aid rules must be checked individually.

name: Founder's, Trustees' and Dean's scholarships
value: Founder’s and Trustees’ awards: full or half tuition. Dean’s awards: $15,000–$25,000 per year. Renewable up to eight consecutive semesters, or ten for a bona fide five-year program.
deadline: Admission Early Decision I November 1; Early Decision II or Regular Decision January 1. Current cycle years are not explicit. These merit awards have no separate application deadline.
apply: Automatic consideration through Common App or Coalition with Scoir, including Lehigh questions/writing supplement, official transcript and school report with counselor recommendation, one teacher recommendation, and midyear/final reports as applicable. SAT/ACT scores are optional indefinitely. International applicants follow English-proficiency and financial-certification requirements.
eligibility: Full-time admitted students considered for exceptional academic achievement and leadership. No numeric entry GPA floor is published. Renewal requires at least 3.0 cumulative GPA and full-time undergraduate enrollment.
notes: Founder’s, Trustees’ and Dean’s are distinct Lehigh merit awards grouped here with their different published values. Admission automatically provides consideration. Current admission page does not label the Fall 2027 year for its November 1 and January 1 deadlines.
